mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the rate environment supports higher present values of future cash flows.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 8.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate profit visibility, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 8.5% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) below their 12-month moving averages signals broad-based consumer demand weakness, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS are below their 12-month moving averages over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle contraction regime (INDPRO < 95.0), declining industrial output signals reduced corporate production capacity and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as market participants price in economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for PAYEMS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% per annum signals rising inflation that may prompt monetary tightening, compressing equity valuations through higher discount rates and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 and real GDP growth (GDPC1) below 0.5% year-over-year signals a deepening economic slowdown, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate output and earnings visibility.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0 and GDPC1 YoY growth < 0.5% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During strong labor market growth (PAYEMS month-over-month growth > 0.5%), rising employment supports consumer spending and corporate profit momentum, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as market participants anticipate sustained economic expansion.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS MoM growth > 0.5% over a 3-year rolling window.
